additional_concerns: The request-only formula answers duty activation under the candidate's stated reading; TRUE does not establish fulfillment or SFC satisfaction. The label TRUE_IS_SATISFIED must not be interpreted as substantive compliance.

Footnote 5 omits the request qualification when mentioning demonstration. Reading it as specifying content is supported by paragraph 14's syntax, but an independent demonstration obligation remains a rival reading requiring resolution before treating the formula as exhaustive.
The complete requirements of paragraphs 10–13 are not supplied. Neither minimum demonstration content nor the reach of the high-confidence qualification can be settled from these excerpts alone.
Paragraphs 15 and 16 concern distinct requested actions. A paragraph 14 demonstration request does not automatically require an audit, verification or legal opinion.

Proper records and operational compatibility are substantive duties distinct from retained accountability. UT Code 6.8 permits an allocated register-maintenance role; it does not establish discharge of the Product Provider's responsibility. Its separate address-notification request is not the paragraph 14 trigger.

UT Code 6.11C supplies a valuation-specific supervision standard, not an established tokenisation safe harbour. Practical authority or supervisory conduct cannot become a sufficient accountability test without an applicable standard and actual evidence.
The supplied structural and retrieval results establish neither legal applicability nor factual satisfaction. No actual SFC request or provider conduct is established by the packet.
